\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{بوتل} (botal)}{بوتل (botal)}]{\ur{بوتل} (botal) — a bottle}

\label{lesson:UR-C61-botal}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a knife, then the Urdu for a fork; a thorn.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{بوتل}}
\textbf{\ur{بوتل}} — \emph{botal} — \textquotedblleft{}a bottle\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{بوتل}} (\emph{botal}) is usually traced to English \emph{bottle}; some trace it to Portuguese \emph{botelha}, \textquotedblleft{}bottle\textquotedblright{}, which reached India first. CDIAL has no entry for it.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{botal}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{botal}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a knife, then the Urdu for a fork; a thorn, then say \emph{botal} again
\end{itemize}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{کتاب} (kitāb)}{کتاب (kitāb)}]{\ur{کتاب} (kitāb) — a book}

\label{lesson:UR-C61-kitab}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a fork; a thorn, then the Urdu for a bottle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{کتاب}}
\textbf{\ur{کتاب}} — \emph{kitāb} — \textquotedblleft{}a book\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{کتاب}} (\emph{kitāb}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{kitāb}, \textquotedblleft{}book, writing\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{k-t-b} (Lane). The same root gives \emph{kātib}, \textquotedblleft{}scribe\textquotedblright{}, and \emph{maktab}, \textquotedblleft{}school, office\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

\raggedright

  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kitāb}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{kitāb}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a fork; a thorn, then the Urdu for a bottle, then say \emph{kitāb} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{کتاب} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A book\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اخبار} (akhbār)}{اخبار (akhbār)}]{\ur{اخبار} (akhbār) — a newspaper}

\label{lesson:UR-C61-akhbar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a book, then the Urdu for a pen.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اخبار}}
\textbf{\ur{اخبار}} — \emph{akhbār} — \textquotedblleft{}a newspaper\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اخبار}} (\emph{akhbār}) is a loan from Arabic \emph{akhbār}, \textquotedblleft{}reports, news\textquotedblright{}, which reached Urdu through Persian. Its Arabic root is \emph{kh-b-r} (Lane). It is the plural of \emph{khabar}, \textquotedblleft{}news\textquotedblright{}; Urdu uses it for the paper that carries them.
\end{cousinweb}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{اسکول} (iskūl)}{اسکول (iskūl)}]{\ur{اسکول} (iskūl) — a school}

\label{lesson:UR-C61-iskul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a pen, then the Urdu for a newspaper.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{اسکول}}
\textbf{\ur{اسکول}} — \emph{iskūl} — \textquotedblleft{}a school\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{اسکول}} (\emph{iskūl}) is a loan from English \emph{school}. English had it from Latin \emph{schola}, and Latin from Greek \emph{skholē}, \textquotedblleft{}leisure\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}
